documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy
documents.summary: A short provost-issued policy effective August 2024. It sets no default for AI use and instead makes faculty responsible for deciding whether, when and how AI is used, requires them to say so in syllabi, and makes students responsible for following it. Units may adopt stricter policies; the CTL supplies sample statements from prohibited to unrestricted.
documents.stance_why: The policy states "Faculty are responsible for deciding whether, when, and how generative AI is used in courses, programs, and/or research" and sets no default allow or ban, so it delegates to instructors; units may only be "more restrictive".

units.why: The purpose statement says it exists "to provide guidance on the responsible use of generative AI", an institution-level framing; coded P56 (framework/purpose) because it sets purpose rather than a rule, so informs/neutral.
units.anchor: The purpose of this policy is to provide guidance on the responsible use of generative

units.why: The definition "the ability of a machine to perform cognitive functions associated with human minds" fixes what the policy covers, so it is P61 (define AI), informs.
units.anchor: the ability of a machine to perform cognitive functions associated with human minds

units.why: "This policy applies to members of the Mercer community who are engaged in academic work and scholarship" sets scope; P61 covers definitions that set what a policy covers, and it binds everyone, general phase, informs.
units.anchor: applies to members of the Mercer community who are engaged in academic work and scholarship

units.why: "Individual units may implement separate generative AI policies" lets units add their own policies; this is institution-level layering (P56), not an instructor-level choice (P04), so P56, addressed to admin units, may.
units.anchor: Individual units may implement separate generative AI policies

units.why: "more restrictive, not less restrictive, than this University policy" makes the university text a floor that units may only tighten; P56 (framework) rather than P04 because it constrains unit policies; the unit_stance is neutral because it sets no stance on AI itself.
units.anchor: more restrictive, not less restrictive, than this University policy

units.why: "must be used responsibly and consistently with academic and professional codes of ethics, standards of citations" states the general principle binding all users; P56 principles fits better than P36 because it names no misconduct or sanction.
units.anchor: Generative AI must be used responsibly and consistently with academic and professional codes of ethics

units.why: "Authors of content generated by AI are responsible for that content" puts ownership on whoever submits; P29 (students own what they submit) fits, though it says authors generally, so actor all.
units.anchor: Authors of content generated by AI are responsible for that content.

units.why: "Faculty are responsible for deciding whether, when, and how generative AI is used" hands the decision to instructors, the core delegation, P04, a duty for faculty at design time.
units.anchor: Faculty are responsible for deciding whether, when, and how generative AI is used

units.why: "Faculty must clearly communicate generative AI use to students in course syllabi, assignment instructions" requires AI expectations in syllabi, P09, at course start.
units.anchor: Faculty must clearly communicate generative AI use to students in course syllabi, assignment instructions

units.why: "Students are responsible for understanding and adhering to faculty communications" binds students to each instructor's rule; P04 (instructor sets the rule) is the best home since the student duty follows from the delegation; P29 does not fit as it is about adherence, not owning work.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for understanding and adhering to faculty communications

units.why: "provides example syllabus statements on generative AI for faculty consideration, ranging from strictly prohibited use of AI to unrestricted use" offers faculty support materials; P63 (support faculty) fits, informs.

documents.title: Sample Syllabus and Assignment Guidance for AI Use
documents.summary: A CTL guide that tells faculty how to write course-level and assignment-level AI statements, with Red/Yellow/Green sample language, a recommended baseline that bans AI unless an assignment permits it, and sections on disclosure, privacy, equitable access and why detector scores are not proof. It is a template, not a rule imposed on students.
